sentences.zh: 調宛平。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Wanping.

sentences.zh: 盧溝橋有逆旅，多陰戕過客沒其財，峨發其奸。

translations.literal: At Lugou Bridge there was an inn where travelers were often secretly murdered and robbed of their property; E exposed the crime.
translations.idiomatic: At Lugou Bridge there was an inn where travelers were often secretly murdered and robbed of their goods; E exposed the crime.

sentences.zh: 西山煤礦多藏匿亡命，峨散其黨與，先後捕治置諸法。

translations.literal: The Western Hills coal mines sheltered many fugitives; E broke up their gangs and in succession arrested and punished them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Hills coal mines sheltered many fugitives; E broke up their gangs and in succession arrested and punished them according to law.

sentences.zh: 三遷通永道，以母憂歸。

translations.literal: Promoted three times to Tongyong Circuit intendant, he returned home upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted three times to Tongyong Circuit intendant, he returned home upon his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 起天津道，仍調通永道，以父憂歸。

translations.literal: Recalled as Tianjin Circuit intendant, again transferred to Tongyong Circuit intendant, he returned home upon his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Tianjin Circuit intendant and again transferred to Tongyong Circuit intendant, he returned home upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 未一年，上命署清河道，服闋真除。

translations.literal: Within a year the emperor ordered him to serve as acting Qinghe Circuit intendant; when mourning ended he received formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year the emperor ordered him to serve as acting Qinghe Circuit intendant; when mourning ended he received formal appointment.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，遷湖北按察使。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was transferred to provincial surveillance commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he was made provincial surveillance commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 石首有寡婦，兄公謀其產，誣之，死於獄。

translations.literal: In Shishou there was a widow whose elder brother-in-law plotted for her property, framed her, and she died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: In Shishou there was a widow whose elder brother-in-law plotted for her property, framed her, and she died in prison.

sentences.zh: 峨治官書發其枉，逮其兄公至，親鞫，論如律。

translations.literal: E examined the official records, exposed the injustice, had the elder brother-in-law brought in, personally tried the case, and sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: E examined the official records, exposed the injustice, had the elder brother-in-law brought in, personally tried the case, and punished him as the law required.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，遷安徽布政使，調山西。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he was transferred to provincial treasurer of Anhui and then to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year he was made provincial treasurer of Anhui and then transferred to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，擢廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he was promoted to governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he was promoted to governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 甫兩月，遷直隸總督。

translations.literal: After only two months he was transferred to Governor-General of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: After only two months he was transferred to Governor-General of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 輔國公弘晸遣僕至靜海冒佔入官地，事聞，上諭峨：「遇王公以下私遣人幹有司，無問是非曲直，即據實奏聞。」

translations.literal: Prince of the Second Rank Hongchang sent a servant to Jinghai to seize by fraud imperial confiscated land; when the matter was reported the emperor instructed E: "When princes and dukes on down privately send men to interfere with local officials, regardless of right or wrong, report the facts at once.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of the Second Rank Hongchang sent a servant to Jinghai to seize by fraud imperial confiscated land; when the matter was reported the emperor instructed E: "When princes and dukes on down privately send men to interfere with local officials, regardless of right or wrong, report the facts at once.

sentences.zh: 長蘆鹽政徵瑞奏漕艘至楊村，以民船剝運，鹽運遲誤。

translations.literal: The Changlu salt commissioner Zheng Rui memorialized that when the grain transport fleet reached Yangcun, civilian boats were used for lighterage, causing delay in salt transport.
translations.idiomatic: The Changlu salt commissioner Zheng Rui reported that when the grain transport fleet reached Yangcun, civilian boats were employed for lighterage, delaying salt shipments.

sentences.zh: 上謂非特鹽運遲誤，且恐商貨壅滯，令峨赴天津與徵瑞議民船編號輪僱，照例發價，並定赴通回空限期，下部議行。

translations.literal: The emperor said this would not only delay salt transport but also risk blocking commercial goods; he ordered E to go to Tianjin and consult with Zheng Rui on numbering civilian boats for rotation hire, paying standard rates, and setting time limits for journeys to Tongzhou and empty return voyages, submitting the plan to the ministry for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said this would delay not only salt transport but also risk jamming commercial traffic; he ordered E to Tianjin to consult Zheng Rui on numbering civilian boats for rotational hire at standard rates, and on setting deadlines for trips to Tongzhou and empty return voyages, then refer the plan to the ministry for action.

sentences.zh: 分疏劾中倉監督趙元搢嗾毆民至死，三河知縣王治岐挪用旗租，並論如律。

translations.literal: In separate memorials he impeached Zhao Yuanjin, supervisor of the Central Granary, for inciting a beating that killed a commoner, and Wang Zhiqi, magistrate of Sanhe, for embezzling banner rents; both were sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In separate memorials he impeached Zhao Yuanjin, supervisor of the Central Granary, for inciting a beating that killed a commoner, and Wang Zhiqi, magistrate of Sanhe, for embezzling banner rents; both were punished as the law required.

sentences.zh: 謁避暑山莊祝嘏，賜孔雀翎、黃馬褂。

translations.literal: He paid homage at the Mountain Resort to offer birthday felicitations and was granted a peacock feather and a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: He paid homage at the Mountain Resort to offer birthday felicitations and received a peacock feather and a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 南宮民魏玉凱訴縣人李存仁習邪教，上遣侍郎姜晟會鞫。

translations.literal: Wei Yukai, a commoner of Nangong, sued Li Cunren of the county for practicing heterodox teachings; the emperor dispatched Vice Minister Jiang Sheng to join in the trial.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yukai, a man of Nangong, accused Li Cunren of the county of practicing heterodox teachings; the emperor sent Vice Minister Jiang Sheng to assist in the investigation.

sentences.zh: 存仁坐誅，玉凱妄及無辜，論戍。

translations.literal: Cunren was executed; Yukai had falsely implicated the innocent and was sentenced to exile.
translations.idiomatic: Cunren was put to death; Yukai had falsely implicated innocent people and was sentenced to exile.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，上遣尚書金簡會勘盧溝橋下游沙淤，請於中泓五孔抽溝三道。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year the emperor dispatched Minister Jin Jian to inspect jointly the silt at the lower reaches below Lugou Bridge and requested three drainage channels cut through the five central sluice openings.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year the emperor sent Minister Jin Jian to inspect jointly the silt buildup below Lugou Bridge; he proposed cutting three drainage channels through the five central sluice openings.

sentences.zh: 上以抽溝水緩，命中泓五孔全行疏濬。

translations.literal: The emperor held that dredging channels would slow the water and ordered full dredging of all five central sluice openings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged that cutting drainage channels would slacken the flow and ordered complete dredging of all five central sluice openings.

sentences.zh: 徵瑞請捐銀三十萬造剝船濟運，上以直隸木材少，命湖廣、江西二省分造。

translations.literal: Zheng Rui requested donating three hundred thousand taels of silver to build lighter boats to aid transport; the emperor, noting that Zhili had little timber, ordered Huguang and Jiangxi provinces to build them separately.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Rui proposed raising three hundred thousand taels to build lighter boats to aid transport; noting the timber shortage in Zhili, the emperor ordered Huguang and Jiangxi to build them separately.

sentences.zh: 峨奏言：「北倉存漕四十餘萬，俟新造剝船刑齊，先行運通。」

translations.literal: E memorialized: "The Northern Granary holds more than four hundred thousand piculs of tribute grain; when the newly built lighter boats are complete, transport to Tongzhou should proceed first.
translations.idiomatic: E memorialized: "The Northern Granary stores more than four hundred thousand piculs of tribute grain; once the new lighter boats are ready, we should begin shipping them to Tongzhou first.

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 五十一年七月，廣平民段文經、元城民徐克展為亂，夜入大名，戕大名道熊恩紱。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifty-first year, Duan Wenjing of Guangping and Xu Kezhan of Yuancheng raised rebellion, entered Daming by night, and killed Xiong Enfu, intendant of the Daming Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifty-first year, Duan Wenjing of Guangping and Xu Kezhan of Yuancheng rebelled, stole into Daming by night, and killed Xiong Enfu, intendant of the Daming Circuit.

sentences.zh: 峨奏聞，即督兵馳往捕治，得從亂者王國桂等，自列向習八卦教，及文經、克展蓄謀為亂狀。

translations.literal: E reported at once and led troops in haste to arrest and suppress them; rebels such as Wang Guogui were captured and testified that they had formerly practiced the Eight Trigrams teaching and that Wenjing and Kezhan had long plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: E reported immediately and led troops posthaste to suppress the disorder; captured rebels including Wang Guogui testified that they had practiced the Eight Trigrams teaching and that Wenjing and Kezhan had long plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 上令峨捕文經、克展，久之未獲，累降旨詰責。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered E to capture Wenjing and Kezhan; after long failure he repeatedly sent edicts of reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered E to capture Wenjing and Kezhan; when they remained at large for a long time, he repeatedly sent edicts of reprimand.

sentences.zh: 十月，河南巡撫畢沅奏於亳州獲克展，檻送京師，而文經終未能得。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Bi Yuan, governor of Henan, memorialized that Kezhan was captured at Bozhou and sent in a caged cart to the capital, but Wenjing was never captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Governor Bi Yuan of Henan reported that Kezhan had been captured at Bozhou and sent to the capital in a cage cart, but Wenjing was never found.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，命停峨本年廉俸。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was ordered to suspend E's salary for that year.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year the emperor ordered E's salary for that year suspended.

sentences.zh: 山東學政劉權之迎眷屬赴官，途遇盜，峨坐奪官，命留任。

translations.literal: Liu Quanzhi, educational commissioner of Shandong, was bringing his family to his post when he met bandits on the road; E was held accountable and stripped of his post but ordered to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: Educational Commissioner Liu Quanzhi of Shandong was bringing his family to his post when bandits attacked on the road; E was stripped of his post for negligence but ordered to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，命偕山東巡撫長麟等勘議糧艘在德州剝運。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year he was ordered together with Chang Lin, governor of Shandong, and others to inspect and deliberate on lighterage of grain fleets at Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year he was ordered, together with Governor Chang Lin of Shandong and others, to inspect and decide on lighterage of grain fleets at Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，巡城御史穆克登額等獲建昌盜，自列嘗劫建昌錢鋪，有同為盜者，系清苑獄二年未決。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year City-Patrol Censor Mukedenge and others captured a bandit of Jianchang who confessed to having robbed a money shop in Jianchang; a fellow bandit had been held in Qingyuan prison for two years without judgment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year City-Patrol Censor Mukedenge and others captured a Jianchang bandit who confessed to robbing a money shop there; an accomplice had languished two years in Qingyuan prison without trial.

sentences.zh: 上責峨廢弛，遣侍衛慶成逮清苑知縣米复松詣京師，下刑部論罪；

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked E for lax administration, dispatched Guard Qingcheng to bring Mi Fusong, magistrate of Qingyuan, to the capital, and referred him to the Ministry of Punishments for sentencing;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked E for lax administration, sent Guard Qingcheng to bring Qingyuan Magistrate Mi Fusong to the capital, and had the Ministry of Punishments try him;

sentences.zh: 奪峨孔雀翎、黃馬褂，降調兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: E's peacock feather and yellow riding jacket were revoked and he was demoted and transferred to vice minister of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: E lost his peacock feather and yellow riding jacket and was demoted to vice minister of the Board of War.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to minister.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，命如河南按虞城民訴縣役事，又如江西按廣豐武弁包漕、崇義民發塚棄骸事，並訊明，論如律。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he was ordered to go to Henan to investigate a commoner's complaint against a county runner, and again to Jiangxi to investigate a military officer of Guangfeng monopolizing grain transport and commoners of Chongyi desecrating graves and discarding remains; in each case he examined the facts and sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year he was sent to Henan to investigate a commoner's complaint against a county runner, and to Jiangxi to investigate a Guangfeng military officer who monopolized grain transport and Chongyi commoners who opened graves and discarded remains; he established the facts in each case and punished the offenders as the law required.

sentences.zh: 峨至崇義，入深山中勘塚地，江西民稱之。

translations.literal: When E reached Chongyi he entered deep mountains to inspect grave sites, and the people of Jiangxi praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When E reached Chongyi he went into the deep mountains to inspect grave sites, and the people of Jiangxi praised him.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，從上幸熱河，賜還孔雀翎、黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he accompanied the emperor to Rehe and was restored the peacock feather and yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year he accompanied the emperor to Rehe and had his peacock feather and yellow riding jacket restored.

sentences.zh: 六十年，以疾乞解任，加太子少保，原品休致。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year, citing illness he requested retirement; he was given the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and retired at his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he asked to retire on grounds of illness; he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and retired at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 卒，賜祭葬，諡恪簡。

translations.literal: Upon his death he was granted funeral rites and the posthumous name Kéjiǎn.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was granted funeral honors; his posthumous name was Kéjiǎn.

sentences.zh: 陸耀，字青來，江南吳江人。

translations.literal: Lu Yao, styled Qinglai, was a native of Wujiang in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yao, whose style was Qinglai, came from Wujiang in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十七年舉人。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Qianlong he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the seventeenth year of Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 十九年，考授內閣中書，充軍機處章京。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed by examination as a Secretariat drafter and served as a clerk in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he passed the examination for Secretariat drafter and served as a clerk in the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 奉職勤慎，有急務立辦，大學士傅恆深器之。

translations.literal: Diligent and careful in office, he handled urgent business at once; Grand Secretary Fu Heng greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent and careful in office, he disposed of urgent business at once; Grand Secretary Fu Heng held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 上出巡幸，俱令扈從。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went on tour he was always ordered to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went on tour, Yao was always ordered to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，出為雲南大理知府，以親老請改補近省，調山東登州府。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he went out as prefect of Dali in Yunnan; citing aged parents he requested transfer to a nearer province and was assigned to Dengzhou prefecture in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year he was appointed prefect of Dali in Yunnan; citing aged parents he asked for a nearer post and was transferred to Dengzhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，調濟南府。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was transferred to Jinan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year he was transferred to Jinan.

sentences.zh: 上書巡撫徐績，請留南漕廣積貯。

translations.literal: He wrote to Governor Xu Ji requesting that southern tribute grain be retained in larger stores.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Governor Xu Ji urging larger reserves of southern tribute grain.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，授甘肅西寧道。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was appointed intendant of Xining Circuit in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he was made intendant of Xining Circuit in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 燿乞績代奏，乞假送母居京師，上命改授運河道。

translations.literal: Yao asked Ji to submit on his behalf a request for leave to escort his mother to residence in the capital; the emperor ordered him transferred instead to the Grain Transport Circuit intendant post.
translations.idiomatic: Yao asked Ji to submit for him a request for leave to settle his mother in the capital; the emperor transferred him instead to Grain Transport Circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 上書河道總督姚立德，言：「兗州、泰安二府泉四百七十八，當濬渠導泉，俾由高趨下，其流不絕。」

translations.literal: He wrote to Grand Canal Commissioner Yao Lide: "The four hundred seventy-eight springs in Yanzhou and Tai'an prefectures should have channels dredged to conduct the springs so that flowing from high to low their streams never cease.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Grand Canal Commissioner Yao Lide: "Of the four hundred seventy-eight springs in Yanzhou and Tai'an prefectures, channels should be dredged to conduct the water downhill so the flow never fails.

sentences.zh: 又言：「運河例歲冬閉壩，春挑濬，天寒晷短，民役俱憊。

translations.literal: He also said: "By custom the Grand Canal sluices are closed in winter and dredged in spring; in cold weather with short days both laborers and corvée workers are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "By custom the canal sluices are closed in winter and dredged in spring; in the cold, with short days, corvée laborers are worn out.

sentences.zh: 宜修復南旺、濟寧、臨清月河，並於彭口南岸亦開月河。

translations.literal: The auxiliary channels at Nanwang, Jining, and Linqing should be restored, and an auxiliary channel should also be opened on the south bank at Pengkou.
translations.idiomatic: The auxiliary channels at Nanwang, Jining, and Linqing should be restored, and an auxiliary channel opened on the south bank at Pengkou as well.

sentences.zh: 歲九、十月漕艘商舶皆從此行，以其時疏濬運河。」

translations.literal: In the ninth and tenth months each year grain fleets and merchant vessels would all use these routes, dredging the Grand Canal at that season.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the ninth and tenth months grain fleets and merchant vessels would all use these routes, leaving that season free to dredge the canal.

sentences.zh: 皆用其議。

translations.literal: All his proposals were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: All his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 又請修河渠志，成運河備考。

translations.literal: He also requested compiling a gazetteer of rivers and canals, completing the Reference Materials on the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed compiling a gazetteer of rivers and canals, producing the Reference Materials on the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，壽張民王倫為亂，去濟寧二百里，有欲閉城者，燿不可，曰：「寇未至閉城，示之怯也。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year Wang Lun of Shouzhang raised rebellion two hundred li from Jining; some wished to close the city gates but Yao refused, saying: "To close the gates before the rebels arrive shows cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year Wang Lun of Shouzhang rebelled two hundred li from Jining; some wanted to shut the gates but Yao refused, saying: "Closing the gates before the enemy arrives shows fear.

sentences.zh: 且何忍拒吾民使散逸被賊害且脅誘耶？」

translations.literal: And how could we bear to shut out our people, leaving them scattered to be harmed and coerced by bandits?
translations.idiomatic: And how could we shut out our own people, leaving them scattered to be harmed or lured by bandits?

sentences.zh: 乃募鄉兵助守，坐城闉任稽察，事旋定。

translations.literal: He then recruited local militia to assist in defense, sat at the city gate to oversee inspection, and the matter was soon settled.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited local militia to help defend the city, sat at the gate to supervise inspection, and order was soon restored.

sentences.zh: 四十年，擢按察使，燿議以流犯罪輕，請免其解司；

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner; Yao proposed that because exile offenses were minor, escort to the provincial office should be waived;
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner; Yao argued that because exile offenses were minor, prisoners need not be escorted to the provincial office;

sentences.zh: 四十三年，擢布政使，燿議流外壅積，請停分發：皆從之。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was promoted to provincial treasurer; Yao proposed that because exile destinations were congested, distribution should be suspended: all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he was promoted to provincial treasurer; Yao proposed suspending further distribution because exile destinations were overcrowded: both requests were granted.

sentences.zh: 燿母老，病狂疾，奏乞解任終養，上許之。

translations.literal: Yao's mother was old and ill with madness; he memorialized requesting retirement to care for her until her death, and the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's mother was old and afflicted with madness; he asked to retire to care for her until her death, and the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 運河築堤，上以燿習河務，命往山東會運河道沈啟震董其役。

translations.literal: When dikes were to be built on the Grand Canal, the emperor, noting Yao's familiarity with river works, ordered him to Shandong to join Grain Transport Circuit Intendant Shen Qizhen in supervising the project.
translations.idiomatic: When dikes were to be built on the canal, the emperor, knowing Yao's expertise in river works, sent him to Shandong to join Grain Transport Circuit Intendant Shen Qizhen in supervising the project.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，命署布政使，服闋真除。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he was ordered to serve as acting provincial treasurer; when mourning ended he received formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he was appointed acting provincial treasurer; when mourning ended he received the post in full.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，擢湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he was promoted to governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year he was promoted to governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 湖南鹽商例有餽，峻卻之，命平鹽價如其數。

translations.literal: Hunan salt merchants customarily offered gifts; he sternly refused them and ordered salt prices reduced by that amount.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan salt merchants customarily offered gifts; he refused them sternly and ordered salt prices cut by the same amount.

sentences.zh: 疏請增岳麓、城南二書院膏火，又疏請申親老告養例，請敕各督撫不論現任、試用，通飭呈明終養。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting increased stipends for the Yuelu and Chengnan academies, and again memorialized to clarify the precedent for retiring to care for aged parents, asking that all governors-general and governors, whether in formal or probationary posts, be uniformly instructed to report when seeking retirement for final nursing.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for increased stipends at the Yuelu and Chengnan academies, and again to clarify the precedent for retiring to care for aged parents, asking that all governors-general and governors, in formal or probationary posts alike, be instructed to report when seeking leave for final nursing care.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「湖南社倉前巡撫劉墉令湘陰等四十五州縣勸捐，得穀十二萬；

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Former Governor Liu Yong of Hunan ordered charity granaries in Xiangyin and forty-four other districts and counties to solicit donations, raising one hundred twenty thousand piculs of grain;
translations.idiomatic: He also reported: "Former Governor Liu Yong ordered charity granaries in Xiangyin and forty-four other districts and counties to solicit donations, raising one hundred twenty thousand piculs of grain;

sentences.zh: 勒限嚴催，僅耒陽等十五州縣交齊，餘未足數者十七縣，全未交者十三縣。

translations.literal: Under strict deadlines and urgent collection, only Leiyang and fourteen other districts and counties paid in full; seventeen fell short of the quota; thirteen had paid nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: Under strict deadlines and pressure to collect, only Leiyang and fourteen other districts and counties paid in full; seventeen fell short; thirteen had paid nothing.

sentences.zh: 如湘陰、巴陵、武陵諸縣濱臨江湖，地多磽瘠；

translations.literal: Counties such as Xiangyin, Baling, and Wuling border lakes and rivers and have much barren land;
translations.idiomatic: Counties such as Xiangyin, Baling, and Wuling border lakes and rivers on land that is mostly poor and thin;

sentences.zh: 桂陽、瀘溪、辰谿諸縣介在山僻，民鮮蓋藏；

translations.literal: Guyang, Luxi, Chenxi, and other counties lie in remote mountains where the people have little stored surplus;
translations.idiomatic: Guyang, Luxi, Chenxi, and other counties lie in remote hills where the people have little surplus to store;

sentences.zh: 若執前捐數目，責令全完，民間未霑借貸之益，轉受追呼之擾。

translations.literal: If the earlier donation quotas were enforced and payment demanded in full, the people would receive none of the benefit of loans from the granaries yet suffer the harassment of collection.
translations.idiomatic: If we insist on the original quotas and demand full payment, the people will never see the benefit of granary loans yet will suffer the harassment of tax collectors.

sentences.zh: 請凡現在未收者停止催繳。」

translations.literal: He requested that all amounts still unpaid cease to be collected.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that collection cease on all amounts still outstanding.

sentences.zh: 上允其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his memorial.

sentences.zh: 燿以病請解任。

translations.literal: Yao requested retirement on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yao asked to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 旋卒。

translations.literal: He soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 燿自幼立志以古人自期，學兼體用。

translations.literal: From youth Yao resolved to measure himself against the ancients; his learning united principle and practice.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yao resolved to measure himself against the ancients; his learning joined theory and practice.

sentences.zh: 居官廉儉。

translations.literal: In office he was incorrupt and frugal.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was incorrupt and frugal.

sentences.zh: 入覲，門吏留裝物索貲；

translations.literal: When he came to court audience, gate attendants detained his luggage and demanded payment;
translations.idiomatic: When he came to audience at court, gate attendants held his luggage and demanded a fee;

sentences.zh: 燿乃置衣被城外而假於友，覲已還之。

translations.literal: Yao therefore left his clothes and bedding outside the city and borrowed from a friend; after the audience he returned them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao left his clothes and bedding outside the city and borrowed from a friend; after the audience he returned them.

sentences.zh: 初至長沙，總督特升額以閱兵至，見翟方午食，惟菽乳蔬蓏，訝之。

translations.literal: When he first reached Changsha, Governor-General Tesheng'e came to review troops and saw Yao at midday meal with only beans, curd, vegetables, and fruit, and was astonished.
translations.idiomatic: When he first reached Changsha, Governor-General Tesheng'e came to review troops and found Yao at midday meal with nothing but beans, curd, vegetables, and fruit, and was astonished.

sentences.zh: 燿曰：「天不雨，方齋，故所食止此。」

translations.literal: Yao said: "Heaven sends no rain; I am just fasting, so my food is only this.
translations.idiomatic: Yao said: "Heaven sends no rain; I am fasting, so this is all I eat.

sentences.zh: 特升額怒其奴曰：「吾館舍酒肉臭，何不以祈雨告？」

translations.literal: Tesheng'e angrily told his servants: "The wine and meat at my lodging stinks—why did you not tell me he was praying for rain?
translations.idiomatic: Tesheng'e angrily rebuked his servants: "The wine and meat at my lodging is going to waste—why didn't you tell me he was fasting for rain?

sentences.zh: 還館舍，命悉撤去。

translations.literal: Returning to his lodging he ordered everything removed.
translations.idiomatic: Back at his lodging he ordered it all cleared away.

sentences.zh: 管幹貞，字松崖，江南陽湖人。

translations.literal: Guan Ganzhen, styled Songya, was a native of Yanghu in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Ganzhen, whose style was Songya, came from Yanghu in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十一年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the thirty-first year of Qianlong, he became a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination in the thirty-first year of Qianlong, became a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 考選貴州道御史。

translations.literal: Selected by examination as censor of the Guizhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected by examination as censor of the Guizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 巡視西城，訟牒皆親判；

translations.literal: Patrolling the Western Ward, he personally judged every petition;
translations.idiomatic: While patrolling the Western Ward he personally decided every case;

sentences.zh: 周行郊內外，捕治諸不法者。

translations.literal: He traveled throughout the suburbs inside and out, arresting and punishing lawbreakers.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled throughout the suburbs inside and outside the city, arresting and punishing offenders.

sentences.zh: 先後命巡漕天津、瓜、儀，凡十二年。

translations.literal: Successively ordered to inspect grain transport at Tianjin, Guazhou, and Yizhen—for twelve years in all.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively ordered to inspect grain transport at Tianjin, Guazhou, and Yizhen—for twelve years in all.

sentences.zh: 累遷至光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 幹貞以漕船回空，多守凍打冰，令先通下游，免上游冰下注，益增堅厚，後遂守其法。

translations.literal: Ganzhen held that when grain boats returned empty many waited for the freeze to break ice; he ordered the lower reaches cleared first to prevent ice from the upper reaches flowing down and growing thicker and harder; afterward this method was always followed.
translations.idiomatic: Ganzhen noted that empty grain boats often waited through the freeze breaking ice; he ordered the lower reaches cleared first so ice from upstream would not descend and grow thicker; afterward this became standard practice.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「運河以諸湖為水櫃，誠使節節疏通，雖遇旱澇，可以節宣。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The Grand Canal relies on the various lakes as water reservoirs; if each section is truly dredged clear, drought and flood can both be regulated.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "The canal depends on its lakes as reservoirs; if every section is kept dredged, drought and flood can both be managed.

sentences.zh: 否則雨少無籌濟之方，雨多無容水之地。

translations.literal: Otherwise when rain is scarce there is no means of supply, and when rain is heavy there is nowhere to hold the water.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise in drought there is no way to supply water, and in flood nowhere to hold it.

sentences.zh: 至引黃入運，系一時權宜。

translations.literal: As for diverting the Yellow River into the canal, that is a temporary expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Diverting the Yellow River into the canal is only a temporary expedient.

sentences.zh: 苟疏濬得宜，黃河全力下注，運河自不致停沙。」

translations.literal: If dredging is properly done, the full force of the Yellow River flowing down will not cause the canal to fill with silt.
translations.idiomatic: With proper dredging, even the full force of the Yellow River flowing downstream will not leave the canal choked with silt.

sentences.zh: 又奏請治駱馬湖，使運河水有所蓄洩，並得旨議行。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting repair of Luoma Lake so canal water would have storage and release, and received imperial approval for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed restoring Luoma Lake so the canal would have storage and outlet, and received imperial approval to deliberate and act.

sentences.zh: 遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year he was promoted to vice minister of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year he was promoted to vice minister of the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，授漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he was appointed Governor of Grain Transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year he was appointed Governor of Grain Transport.

sentences.zh: 糧艘至天津楊村，每以水淺須起撥，運丁不能給舟值，例由長蘆鹽運使以鬻鹽錢貸運丁，借直隸籓庫銀歸款，運丁分年繳納。

translations.literal: When grain fleets reached Tianjin and Yangcun, shallow water often required lighterage; transport coolies could not pay boat fees; by precedent the Changlu salt transport commissioner lent them money from salt sales, borrowing from the Zhili provincial treasury for repayment, with coolies paying in installments over years.
translations.idiomatic: When grain fleets reached Tianjin and Yangcun, shallow water often required lighterage that transport coolies could not afford; by precedent the Changlu salt transport commissioner lent them money from salt sales, drawing on the Zhili provincial treasury for repayment while coolies paid back in installments.

sentences.zh: 其後議停，運丁多不便，幹貞請如舊例。

translations.literal: Later it was proposed to discontinue this; transport coolies found it greatly inconvenient; Ganzhen requested restoration of the old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When discontinuation was later proposed, transport coolies found it a great hardship; Ganzhen asked that the old practice be restored.

sentences.zh: 又疏陳江西軍丁疲敝，請籌款增補，行、月二糧折價；

translations.literal: He also memorialized that Jiangxi military laborers were exhausted and requested funds to supplement them, converting marching and monthly rations to cash;
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that Jiangxi military laborers were exhausted and proposed funds to replenish them, converting marching and monthly grain rations to cash;

sentences.zh: 借官銀代償積逋，令分年輸納；

translations.literal: Borrowing official silver to repay accumulated arrears and requiring payment in installments over years;
translations.idiomatic: Official silver to repay accumulated arrears in installments;

sentences.zh: 寬限清釐屯田，俾藉以調劑。

translations.literal: Extending deadlines for clearing military colony lands so these measures could serve as relief.
translations.idiomatic: And extended deadlines for clearing military colony lands so these measures could provide relief.

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，賜孔雀翎、黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year he was granted a peacock feather and a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year he received a peacock feather and a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 疏言；

translations.literal: He memorialized;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized:

sentences.zh: 「漕艘百餘幫，役夫數万人，最易藏奸生事。

translations.literal: "More than a hundred grain fleet groups with tens of thousands of laborers are the easiest place to hide mischief and breed trouble.
translations.idiomatic: "More than a hundred grain fleet groups employ tens of thousands of laborers—the easiest place for wrongdoing to hide and trouble to breed.

sentences.zh: 上年新漕，飭嚴立規條，行必按伍，止則支更。

translations.literal: Last year for the new tribute grain strict regulations were enforced: when moving they must march in squads; when stopping they must stand watch in shifts.
translations.idiomatic: Last year, for the new tribute grain, strict rules were enforced: on the march they had to move in squads; at rest they had to stand watch in shifts.

sentences.zh: 親行督察，乃知別有姦人隨運潛行。

translations.literal: When he personally went to inspect he then learned that other scoundrels were secretly traveling alongside the transport.
translations.idiomatic: When he inspected in person he discovered that other wrongdoers were secretly traveling alongside the convoys.

sentences.zh: 督飭捕治數十人，交州縣確擬嚴懲。」

translations.literal: He supervised and ordered the arrest and punishment of several dozen people, turning them over to the prefecture and county for confirmed severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the arrest of several dozen offenders and referred them to local authorities for formal sentences of strict punishment.

sentences.zh: 得旨嘉獎。

translations.literal: He received an imperial edict commending him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded with praise.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，疏言：「蘇州太倉押運官，例抵淮後改委赴通。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, he memorialized: "The grain convoy supervisors of Suzhou and Taicang, by precedent, upon reaching the Huai region are reassigned to proceed to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 58 he submitted a memorial: "Suzhou and Taicang convoy officers, by custom, are replaced with new appointees at the Huai when they should continue on to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 中途分更，互相推諉。

translations.literal: Midway they change shifts and pass blame to one another.
translations.idiomatic: En route they hand off duty at intervals and shift responsibility onto each other.

sentences.zh: 請自水次抵通，始終其事，庶官有專司。」

translations.literal: He requested that from the waterfront landing to Tongzhou one official oversee the entire task, so that each office would have dedicated responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that a single officer handle the run from the quay to Tongzhou start to finish, so duties would have clear charge.

sentences.zh: 又請河南豁免緩徵，停運減存船隻，就近赴山東受僱撥運。

translations.literal: He also requested exemption from deferred collection in Henan, suspension of transport with reduction of stored vessels, and hiring nearby in Shandong for allocation and transport.
translations.idiomatic: He also sought deferrals on Henan tax arrears, reduced idle fleets during transport suspensions, and local Shandong hiring for reallocating grain shipments.

sentences.zh: 又請各幫水手短纖，責成頭舵工丁以素識誠實之人充補，免聚眾竊盜諸累。

translations.literal: He also requested that where convoy crews were short-handed, head helmsmen and crew chiefs be charged with filling gaps with persons known to them as honest, to avoid the troubles of mass theft and robbery.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that when crews ran short, head helmsmen recruit replacements from people they knew to be trustworthy, averting the theft and riot problems that came with untested recruits.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All proposals were accepted.

sentences.zh: 各省開兌，多至春初，又在在逗遛，遇水淺或河溢，有在河北度歲者。

translations.literal: When the provinces began grain exchange, it often did not come until early spring; everywhere there was lingering delay; when waters were shallow or rivers flooded, some spent the New Year north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial convoys often did not begin exchange until early spring, dawdling at every stop; in low water or floods some crews spent the winter north of the river.

sentences.zh: 幹貞嚴飭弁丁修艌受兌，复冬兌春開舊制。

translations.literal: Gan Zhen strictly ordered officers and transport workers to repair barges and receive exchange, restoring the old system of winter exchange and spring departure.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhen strictly ordered officers and crews to repair vessels and take on grain, restoring the old winter-exchange, spring-departure schedule.

sentences.zh: 糧艘起運，每策馬督催，風雨不避。

translations.literal: When grain barges set out, he spurred his horse to supervise and press them forward, never shirking wind or rain.
translations.idiomatic: When the grain fleet sailed, he rode alongside to drive them on through wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 或不歸所乘舟，支帳露宿。

translations.literal: Sometimes he did not return to the boat he had been riding, but spread his bedding and slept in the open.
translations.idiomatic: At times he never returned to his own vessel, sleeping outdoors on a mat instead.

sentences.zh: 微弁出力，必親慰勞。

translations.literal: When junior officers exerted themselves even slightly, he personally came to comfort and commend them.
translations.idiomatic: The slightest effort from a petty officer drew his personal thanks and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 運丁舟人不用命，立予懲罰。

translations.literal: Transport workers and boatmen who disobeyed orders were punished on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Transport workers who defied orders were punished immediately.

sentences.zh: 當時或苦其苛急，及回空省費，無絲毫派累，咸大悅服。

translations.literal: At the time some found his severity hard to bear, but when the empty return saved expenses with not the slightest extra levy, all were greatly pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Some grumbled at his harshness at first, yet on the empty return they found costs cut with no hidden charges, and all came round wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘗召見褒其能，謂可亞楊錫紱。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong once summoned him and praised his ability, saying he ranked second only to Yang Xibo.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong summoned him and praised his competence, declaring him second only to Yang Xibo.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，以疾乞假，命兩江總督書麟攝其事。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year, he requested leave for illness; the Two Jiangs Governor-General Shu Lin was ordered to administer his duties.
translations.idiomatic: In year 59 he took sick leave; Governor-General Shu Lin of the Two Jiangs was appointed to act in his stead.

sentences.zh: 疾愈，任事如故。

translations.literal: When his illness abated, he resumed his duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: Once recovered, he returned to duty as before.

sentences.zh: 幹貞成進士時，禮部改「貞」為「珍」，六十年，命仍原名。

translations.literal: When Gan Zhen passed the jinshi examination, the Ministry of Rites changed the character in his name from Zhen (meaning "chastity") to Zhenzhen (meaning "precious"); in the sixtieth year he was ordered to use his original name.
translations.idiomatic: When Gan Zhen passed the jinshi, the Ministry of Rites altered the character in his name from Zhen (chastity) to Zhenzhen (precious); in year sixty the throne ordered him to restore the original form.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，戶部議江、浙白糧全運京倉，以羨米為耗，浙江運丁如議交運。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, the Ministry of Revenue proposed that Jiangsu and Zhejiang white grain be fully transported to Beijing granaries, with surplus grain counted as transport loss; Zhejiang transport workers complied and delivered as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1 the Ministry of Revenue proposed shipping all Jiangsu and Zhejiang tribute rice to Beijing granaries, counting surplus as transport loss; Zhejiang crews complied.

sentences.zh: 幹貞以江南餘米較少，執議不行，交部嚴議，奪官。

translations.literal: Gan Zhen, because Jiangnan had relatively less surplus grain, held to his objections and would not implement it; the matter was referred to the ministry for severe review and his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhen objected that Jiangnan had too little surplus grain to comply; the ministry censured him severely and stripped his rank.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he died.

sentences.zh: 子遹群，官浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: His son Youqun served as Zhejiang governor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Youqun became governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 蔣兆奎，字聚五，陝西渭南人。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhaokui, style Juwu, a native of Weinan in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhaokui, courtesy name Juwu, from Weinan, Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 自副貢生補甘肅張掖縣教諭。

translations.literal: From deputy tribute student he was appointed instructor of Zhangye County in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: A deputy tribute student, he was appointed county instructor of Zhangye in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十一年，成進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Qianlong, he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 31 he earned his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，教諭俸滿，授四川合江知縣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, when his instructor term was complete, he was appointed magistrate of Hejiang in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 33, his instructor term complete, he was made magistrate of Hejiang, Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 調灌縣，丁憂。

translations.literal: Transferred to Guan County, then mourned a parent's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Guan County, then entered mourning.

sentences.zh: 師徵小金川，攻熱耳，總督富勒渾奏留兆奎從軍，駐達烏圍治餉。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned against Lesser Jinchuan and attacked Re'er, Governor-General Fulehun memorialized to retain Zhao-kui with the army, stationing him at Dawuwei to manage supplies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Lesser Jinchuan campaign at Re'er, Governor-General Fulehun kept Zhao-kui with the army, posting him at Dawuwei to manage rations.

sentences.zh: 既破熱耳，移餉往。

translations.literal: Once Re'er was taken, he moved supplies there.
translations.idiomatic: After Re'er fell, he shifted supplies forward.

sentences.zh: 俄，大金川助亂，兆奎知熱耳不足守，复移糧達烏圍。

translations.literal: Soon Greater Jinchuan joined the rebellion; Zhao-kui knew Re'er could not be held and again moved grain back to Dawuwei.
translations.idiomatic: When Greater Jinchuan rose, Zhao-kui judged Re'er indefensible and pulled supplies back to Dawuwei.

sentences.zh: 已而，他所糧悉被焚。

translations.literal: Before long, grain at other locations was entirely burned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward grain stored elsewhere was burned entirely.

sentences.zh: 將軍阿桂才兆奎，使駐日隆治餉，兼司令砲局。

translations.literal: General Agui valued Zhao-kui and had him stationed at Rilong to manage supplies, also commanding the artillery bureau.
translations.idiomatic: General Agui valued him and posted him at Rilong to manage supplies while directing the artillery bureau.

sentences.zh: 旋調署華陽，加知州銜。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to act as magistrate of Huayang, with the additional rank of prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting magistrate of Huayang with prefectural rank added.

sentences.zh: 四川盜號啯嚕子，擾尤溪。

translations.literal: A Sichuan bandit called Guluizi harassed Youxi.
translations.idiomatic: A Sichuan outlaw known as Guluizi raided Youxi.

sentences.zh: 兆奎捕得盜渠，獲首犯。

translations.literal: Zhao-kui captured the bandit ringleaders and seized the chief culprit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao-kui seized the gang leaders and the chief offender.

sentences.zh: 服闋，遷山西澤州同知。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was promoted to sub-prefect of Zezhou in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was promoted to sub-prefect of Zezhou, Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 擢太原知府。

translations.literal: Promoted to prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 以巡撫農起薦，擢河東鹽運使。

translations.literal: On recommendation of Governor Nong Qi, promoted to salt transport commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Nong Qi recommended him for promotion to Hedong salt commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，遷按察使，仍兼理鹽務。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, transferred to provincial judge, still concurrently managing salt affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 54 he became provincial judge while retaining charge of salt.

sentences.zh: 尋遷甘肅布政使。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to financial commissioner of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made financial commissioner of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，高宗八旬萬壽，兆奎入祝嘏。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year, on Emperor Gaozong's eightieth birthday, Zhao-kui came to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In year 56, for the emperor's eightieth birthday, Zhao-kui traveled to court to offer felicitations.

sentences.zh: 時河東商困，兆奎議改鹽課歸地丁，上命如山西同巡撫馮光熊勘議。

translations.literal: At the time Hedong merchants were distressed; Zhao-kui proposed shifting salt levies onto land tax quotas; the emperor ordered joint investigation with Shanxi Governor Feng Guangxiong as in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: With Hedong merchants in distress, Zhao-kui proposed folding salt taxes into land quotas; the throne ordered a joint survey with Shanxi Governor Feng Guangxiong.

sentences.zh: 旋議山西、陝西、河南三省應納正雜課四十八萬餘兩，均入三省行鹽完課納稅百七十二廳州縣地丁，兩加九分有奇，下部議行。

translations.literal: Soon it was proposed that the regular and miscellaneous levies of more than 480,000 taels owed by Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Henan be distributed into the land-tax quotas of 172 subprefectures, counties, and districts in the three provinces where salt was sold and taxes collected, adding a bit more than nine fen per two mu, and submitted to the ministry for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: A plan followed to spread more than 480,000 taels in regular and miscellaneous salt dues across land-tax registers in 172 districts of Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Henan, adding slightly more than nine fen per two mu, and sent to the ministry for approval.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，上以河東鹽價減，銷暢，兩三月內，發販鹽數倍於往年，商民交便。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year, because Hedong salt prices were reduced and sales flourished, within two or three months the volume of salt distributed for sale was several times that of previous years; merchants and people found it mutually convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In year 57, lower Hedong salt prices drove brisk sales; within two or three months distribution exceeded prior years several times over, to merchants' and commoners' mutual benefit.

sentences.zh: 褒兆奎始終承辦，收效甚速，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: Zhao-kui was praised for overseeing the reform from start to finish with very rapid results, and was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Zhao-kui for shepherding the reform through with swift results and awarded him a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 旋授山西巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Shanxi governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，迎蹕，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year, he welcomed the imperial procession and was granted a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: In year 59 he met the imperial tour and received a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 六十年，以山西錢賤，請停寶晉局鑄錢，從之。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year, because Shanxi coin was cheap, he requested suspension of coin minting at the Baojin bureau; approved.
translations.idiomatic: In year 60, with Shanxi copper cash debased, he asked to halt minting at the Baojin foundry and was obliged.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，詔與千叟宴。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing year 1, he was summoned to the Feast of a Thousand Elders.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1 he was invited to the Feast of a Thousand Elders.

sentences.zh: 尋命毋詣京師，仍加恩賚。

translations.literal: Soon ordered not to come to the capital, yet still granted imperial favors.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon excused from traveling to Beijing but still received imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 奏劾汾州知府張力行挾訟事婪索，冀寧道鄧希曾等回護同官。

translations.literal: He memorialized impeaching Fenzhou Prefect Zhang Lixing for extortion using litigation, and Jining Circuit Intendant Deng Xiceng and others for shielding a colleague.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Fenzhou Prefect Zhang Lixing for using lawsuits to extort bribes, and Circuit Intendant Deng Xiceng and others for covering for a fellow official.

sentences.zh: 奪力行官，命兆奎授鞫。

translations.literal: Zhang Lixing was stripped of office; Zhao-kui was ordered to conduct the investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Lixing was dismissed and Zhao-kui appointed to hear the case.

sentences.zh: 又發力行侵帑狀，坐斬。

translations.literal: Further evidence emerged of Lixing's embezzlement from the treasury; he was sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Further proof of Lixing's treasury embezzlement surfaced; he was condemned to decapitation.

sentences.zh: 二年，以病乞解任，歸。

translations.literal: In the second year, he requested release from office due to illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he resigned on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 四年，高宗崩，兆奎入臨，即授漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Emperor Gaozong died; Zhao-kui came to mourn and was immediately appointed Grain Transport Governor-General.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, after Gaozong's death, Zhao-kui came to mourn and was immediately made Grain Transport Governor-General.

sentences.zh: 固辭，不許。

translations.literal: He firmly declined but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He declined firmly but was overruled.

sentences.zh: 旋奏言：「整頓漕運，要在卹丁。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized: "To reform grain transport, the key lies in caring for the transport workers.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized: "Reforming the grain levy depends above all on relieving the banner crews.

sentences.zh: 今陋規盡革，旗丁自可節費；

translations.literal: Now that corrupt customs are entirely abolished, banner sailors can naturally economize;
translations.idiomatic: With abusive fees abolished, banner crews can economize;

sentences.zh: 而生齒日繁，諸物昂貴，旗丁應得之項，實不敷用，急須調劑。

translations.literal: yet mouths multiply daily and all goods are costly; what banner sailors ought to receive is truly insufficient for use, and urgent adjustment is needed.
translations.idiomatic: yet mouths to feed multiply and prices rise; what crews are entitled to no longer suffices, and urgent relief is needed.

sentences.zh: 前讀上諭：'有漕州縣，無不浮收，江、浙尤甚，每石加至七八斗。

translations.literal: Previously reading Your Majesty's edict: 'Among counties handling the grain levy, none fail to over-collect; Jiangsu and Zhejiang are especially severe, adding as much as seven or eight dou per shi.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Your Majesty's earlier edict: 'Grain-levy counties everywhere over-collect; Jiangsu and Zhejiang worst of all, adding seven or eight dou per shi.

sentences.zh: '歷來交納，視為固然。

translations.literal: Through the ages payment has been regarded as a matter of course.
translations.idiomatic: Payment at such rates has long been taken for granted.

sentences.zh: 今若劃出一斗津貼旗丁，餘悉革除。

translations.literal: If now one dou were set aside as stipend for banner sailors and all the rest abolished,
translations.idiomatic: If one dou per shi were earmarked as crew stipend and the rest abolished altogether,

sentences.zh: 所出有限，所省已多。

translations.literal: what was spent would be limited and what was saved would already be great.
translations.idiomatic: the cost would be modest and the savings enormous.

sentences.zh: 不特千萬旗丁藉資濟運，即交糧億萬花戶皆沾恩無窮。」

translations.literal: Not only would tens of millions of banner sailors gain support to sustain transport, but the countless millions of taxpaying households delivering grain would share boundless imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of millions of banner crews would gain support, and countless grain-delivering households would share boundless relief.

sentences.zh: 疏入，上嫌事近加賦，飭與有漕省分各督撫另議調劑。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor disliked that it approached a tax increase and ordered each governor in grain-levy provinces to discuss separate adjustments.
translations.idiomatic: The throne disliked its resemblance to a tax hike and ordered grain-province governors to devise other remedies.

sentences.zh: 兆奎疏言：「各督撫所議調劑，有名無實。

translations.literal: Zhao-kui memorialized: "The adjustments proposed by the various governors are nominal, not real.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao-kui replied that governors' proposed remedies were empty form without substance.

sentences.zh: 兩江費淳所奏，不敷運費；

translations.literal: What Fei Chun of the Two Jiangs reported did not cover transport costs;
translations.idiomatic: Fei Chun of the Two Jiangs admitted his plan would not cover shipping costs;

sentences.zh: 江蘇擬四升七合，安徽擬二升，焉能有濟？」

translations.literal: Jiangsu proposed four sheng seven he, Anhui proposed two sheng — how could that avail?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu offered four sheng seven he, Anhui two sheng — how could that suffice?

sentences.zh: 因力請罷斥。

translations.literal: And therefore he strongly requested dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore begged to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 上責兆奎粗率，並諭：「加賦斷不可行。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Zhao-kui for rashness and also instructed: "A tax increase is absolutely impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked his rashness and declared tax increases absolutely forbidden.

sentences.zh: 此外如何設策善後，令再覈議。」

translations.literal: Beyond this, devise policies for good aftermath; order further review and deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He was told to devise workable follow-up measures and reconsider.

sentences.zh: 兆奎奏請：「每船借給銀百兩，於各糧道庫支領，分三年，以旗丁應領之項扣還。

translations.literal: Zhao-kui memorialized requesting: "Each boat be lent one hundred taels of silver, drawn from each grain-route treasury, repaid over three years by deduction from what banner sailors should receive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao-kui proposed lending each vessel one hundred taels from grain-route treasuries, repaid over three years from crew allotments.

sentences.zh: 山東、河南兩省路途較近，減借五十兩；

translations.literal: Shandong and Henan, with shorter routes, would borrow fifty taels less;
translations.idiomatic: Shandong and Henan, with shorter hauls, would borrow fifty taels less;

sentences.zh: 有漕各省本有輕齎，原應徵米，斗折銀五分。

translations.literal: Grain-levy provinces originally had light-transport allowances that should have been collected in grain, converted at five fen of silver per dou;
translations.idiomatic: Grain provinces already levied light-transport allowances in grain, convertible at five fen per dou;

sentences.zh: 請仍徵本色，按照旗丁米數，分給白糧。

translations.literal: he requested collection still in kind, distributed as white grain according to banner sailors' grain allotments.
translations.idiomatic: he asked to collect these in kind and distribute white grain according to crew rations.

sentences.zh: 無輕齎，請通融勻給。」

translations.literal: Where there was no light-transport allowance, he requested flexible equal distribution.
translations.idiomatic: Where no such allowance existed, he asked for flexible equal distribution.

sentences.zh: 上以「所擬損民益丁，巧避加賦之名，仍存加賦之實」，遣侍郎鐵保會淳詳察。

translations.literal: The emperor said the proposal "harmed the people to benefit the sailors, cleverly avoiding the name of a tax increase while preserving its reality," and dispatched Vice Minister Tiebao to join Fei Chun in detailed investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne condemned it as harming taxpayers while benefiting crews — avoiding the label of a tax hike while keeping its substance — and sent Vice Minister Tiebao with Fei Chun to investigate.

sentences.zh: 兆奎又奏：「旗丁運費本有應得之項，惟定在數十百年之前。

translations.literal: Zhao-kui again memorialized: "Banner sailors' transport costs originally had allotted payments, but these were fixed decades or centuries ago.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao-kui argued that crews' transport fees were fixed decades or centuries ago.

sentences.zh: 今物價數倍，費用不敷。

translations.literal: Today prices are several times higher and expenses do not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Prices had multiplied several times over; the allotments no longer covered costs.

sentences.zh: 近年旗丁尚可支持者，以州縣浮收，向索兌費，並折收行月等米，以之貼補一切經費。

translations.literal: In recent years banner sailors could still manage because prefectures and counties over-collected, demanding exchange fees and converting monthly travel grain and the like, using these to subsidize all expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Recently crews had survived only because counties over-collected, demanding exchange fees and converting travel-month grain to cover all costs.

sentences.zh: 今革除漕弊，浮費可省，兌費不能減。

translations.literal: Now that grain levy abuses are abolished, extraneous costs can be saved, but exchange fees cannot be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: With levy abuses purged, waste could be cut, but exchange fees could not be reduced commensurately.

sentences.zh: 臣才識短淺，惟恐貽誤，求上別簡賢員，原從小心敬畏而來，不敵氣質用事。」

translations.literal: Your servant's talent and insight are shallow; I fear causing error and beg Your Majesty to select another worthy. My proposals arose from careful reverence, not from willful temperament — yet I cannot prevail against accusations of stubbornness.
translations.idiomatic: He confessed limited ability, feared failure, and begged the throne to appoint another — insisting his motives were caution, not stubbornness.

sentences.zh: 上即命鐵保代兆奎，召授工部侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered Tiebao to replace Zhao-kui and summoned Zhao-kui to appoint him Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately replaced him with Tiebao and summoned Zhao-kui to appoint him Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 尋授山東巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Shandong governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 御前侍衛明安泰山進香，還京師，奏山東有司私餽銀八百，並及途中營汛墩房坍塌。

translations.literal: Imperial bodyguard Ming'an, returning to the capital after offering incense at Mount Tai, reported that Shandong officials had privately presented him eight hundred taels of silver, and also mentioned collapsed garrison posts and watchtowers along the route.
translations.idiomatic: Bodyguard Ming'an, returning from Mount Tai, reported Shandong officials had given him eight hundred taels privately and noted collapsed garrison posts along the route.

sentences.zh: 上以詰兆奎，兆奎復奏辯，且稱老病，求去。

translations.literal: The emperor interrogated Zhao-kui; Zhao-kui memorialized again in defense and also cited old age and illness, requesting departure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Zhao-kui; he defended himself in a further memorial, citing age and illness, and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 上怒其忿激，念廉名素著，降三品卿銜休致。

translations.literal: The emperor, angered by his contentious tone but mindful of his longstanding reputation for integrity, reduced him to third-rank nominal dignitary and granted retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Angered by his defiance yet mindful of his integrity, the emperor reduced him to third rank and granted retirement.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he died.

sentences.zh: 胡季堂，河南光山人，侍郎煦子。

translations.literal: Hu Jitang, a native of Guangshan in Henan, son of Vice Minister Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Jitang, from Guangshan, Henan, son of Vice Minister Xu.

sentences.zh: 初以廕生授順天府通判，改刑部員外郎，遷郎中。

translations.literal: Initially as a yin student he was appointed vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture, then transferred to vice director in the Ministry of Punishments, promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: A yin-degree holder, he was appointed vice prefect of Shuntian, then transferred to the Ministry of Punishments as vice director and promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 出為甘肅慶陽知府，再遷甘肅按察使，調江蘇。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Qingyang in Gansu, then twice promoted to Gansu provincial judge, transferred to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Qingyang prefect in Gansu, rose to Gansu provincial judge, then transferred to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 江蘇按察使移駐蘇州，而獄猶在江寧，季堂請更置，報可。

translations.literal: The Jiangsu provincial judge moved his station to Suzhou, but prisons remained in Jiangning; Jitang requested relocation and was approved.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiangsu judge relocated to Suzhou while prisons stayed in Jiangning, Jitang petitioned to move them; approved.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十九年，擢刑部侍郎，四十四年，遷尚書。

translations.literal: In Qianlong year 39, promoted to vice minister of punishments; in year 44, transferred to minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 39 he became vice minister of punishments; in 44, minister.

sentences.zh: 季堂屢奉使諸省讞獄，直隸、吉林、江蘇皆一至，山東四至，河南再至。

translations.literal: Jitang repeatedly received imperial commissions to review criminal cases in various provinces: Zhili, Jilin, and Jiangsu once each; Shandong four times; Henan twice.
translations.idiomatic: Jitang repeatedly toured provinces reviewing cases: Zhili, Jilin, and Jiangsu once each; Shandong four times; Henan twice.

sentences.zh: 察得唆訟者嚴治之；

translations.literal: When he found inciters of litigation, he punished them severely;
translations.idiomatic: Instigators of litigation he punished severely;

sentences.zh: 有誣訴，論如律，不稍貸。

translations.literal: false accusers were judged according to law without the slightest leniency.
translations.idiomatic: false accusers were sentenced by law without mercy.

sentences.zh: 初使河南按商丘獄，上諭之曰：「季堂河南人，按本省事尤當秉公持正。

translations.literal: On his first mission to Henan reviewing the Shangqiu case, the emperor instructed him: "Jitang is a Henan man; in handling matters of his native province you must especially uphold fairness and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: On his first Henan mission, reviewing the Shangqiu case, the emperor warned: "As a Henan native, you must be doubly fair in home-province cases.

sentences.zh: 勿以事涉大吏，慮將來報復，稍為瞻顧。」

translations.literal: Do not because the matter involves high officials, fearing future retaliation, show the slightest hesitation."
translations.idiomatic: Do not shrink from cases involving senior officials for fear of future reprisal.

sentences.zh: 商丘民湯秉五迫孀婦劉為妻，劉絕食死。

translations.literal: A Shangqiu commoner Tang Bingwu forced the widow Liu to be his wife; Liu starved herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangqiu, Tang Bingwu forced the widow Liu to marry him; she starved herself to death.

sentences.zh: 其獄已題旌，劉父猶陳訴，並及順刀神拳會民事，察得唆訟者罪之。

translations.literal: The case had already been recommended for imperial commendation, yet Liu's father still filed a complaint, also involving the Shundao Shenquan Society civil dispute; investigation found the litigation instigator and punished him.
translations.idiomatic: Though the case had already been recommended for imperial commendation, Liu's father still petitioned, also raising a civil dispute involving the Shundao Shenquan Society; investigation found who had incited the lawsuit and punished him.

sentences.zh: 使山東按平度獄，州民羅有良與人鬥，誤蹴其母死。

translations.literal: Sent to Shandong to review the Pingdu case: a commoner of the prefecture named Luo Youliang fought with someone and accidentally kicked his mother to death.
translations.idiomatic: On mission to Shandong he reviewed the Pingdu case: a local named Luo Youliang got into a fight and accidentally kicked his mother to death.

sentences.zh: 萊州知府徐大榕原勘無誤，乃坐是奪官，當平反，得旨嘉獎。

translations.literal: Laizhou Prefect Xu Darong's original investigation had been correct, yet he lost his post on that account; this deserved reversal, and an edict praised the decision.
translations.idiomatic: Laizhou Prefect Xu Darong's original investigation had been correct, yet he had lost his post on that account; the case deserved reversal, and an edict commended the outcome.

sentences.zh: 再使山東，暫署巡撫。

translations.literal: Sent to Shandong again, he temporarily served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Shandong again, he served temporarily as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 山東災，請截本省漕米治賑。

translations.literal: Shandong suffered disaster; he requested diverting the province's grain transport rice for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong suffered disaster, he asked to divert the province's grain transport rice for relief.

sentences.zh: 還京師，加太子少保，再兼署兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and again served concurrently as acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, he received the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and again served concurrently as acting Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，授直隸總督，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing he was appointed governor-general of Zhili and granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiaqing he was appointed governor-general of Zhili and granted a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 四年，仁宗親政，季堂疏發和珅罪狀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when Emperor Renzong took personal rule, Jitang memorialized exposing Heshen's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Emperor Renzong took personal rule, Jitang memorialized exposing Heshen's crimes.

sentences.zh: 尋請以籍沒其僕呼什圖米麥萬餘石，分借文安、大城被水村民。

translations.literal: Soon he requested that more than ten thousand piculs of grain and wheat confiscated from Heshen's servant Hushitu be lent in portions to flood-stricken villagers in Wen'an and Dacheng.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked that more than ten thousand piculs of grain and wheat confiscated from Heshen's servant Hushitu be lent in portions to flood-stricken villagers in Wen'an and Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 長新店盜發，上責季堂廢弛，削太子太保，奪孔雀翎。

translations.literal: Tomb robbers struck at Changxindian; the emperor blamed Jitang for negligence, stripped him of Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and revoked his peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When tomb robbers struck at Changxindian, the emperor blamed Jitang for negligence, stripped him of Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and revoked his peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 下吏部議，奪官，去頂帶留任。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Board of Civil Appointments for deliberation: dismissal from office, removal of rank badge but retention of post.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Civil Appointments deliberated and ruled dismissal from office, removal of his rank badge but retention of his post.

sentences.zh: 河南內黃知縣陶象柄獲長新店首盜，季堂奏聞。

translations.literal: Tao Xiangbing, magistrate of Neihuang in Henan, captured the ringleader of the Changxindian robbers; Jitang reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Xiangbing, magistrate of Neihuang in Henan, captured the ringleader of the Changxindian robbers, and Jitang reported it.

sentences.zh: 上嘉季堂不邀功，還頂帶；

translations.literal: The emperor praised Jitang for not claiming credit and restored his rank badge;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Jitang for not claiming credit and restored his rank badge;

sentences.zh: 又獲從犯，還孔雀翎。

translations.literal: When accomplices were also captured, his peacock feather was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When accomplices were also captured, his peacock feather was restored.

sentences.zh: 是時川、楚、陝教匪為亂，五年，季堂奏：「教匪稽誅，臣聞經略額勒登保、參贊德楞泰等由川而楚而陝而甘，數千百里窮追，接戰輒勝。

translations.literal: At this time sect rebels were in revolt in Sichuan, Hubei, and Shaanxi. In the fifth year Jitang memorialized: "The sect rebels have long evaded extermination. Your servant has heard that Frontier Pacification Commissioner E'erdengbao, Assistant Delengtai, and others have pursued them from Sichuan to Hubei to Shaanxi to Gansu across thousands of li, winning every battle they fought.
translations.idiomatic: At that time sect rebels were in revolt in Sichuan, Hubei, and Shaanxi. In the fifth year Jitang memorialized: "The sect rebels have long evaded extermination. I have heard that Frontier Pacification Commissioner E'erdengbao, Assistant Delengtai, and others have pursued them from Sichuan to Hubei to Shaanxi to Gansu across thousands of li, winning every battle they fought.

sentences.zh: 是教匪所恃，不在勢眾而在得間能逃也。

translations.literal: What the sect rebels rely on is not great numbers but finding openings to escape.
translations.idiomatic: What the sect rebels rely on is not great numbers but finding openings to escape.

sentences.zh: 川、楚、陝連界，崇山峻嶺，斷澗深溝，在在險阻。

translations.literal: Sichuan, Hubei, and Shaanxi share borders; lofty mountains and steep ridges, broken ravines and deep gullies—dangerous terrain everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan, Hubei, and Shaanxi share borders of lofty mountains and steep ridges, broken ravines and deep gullies—dangerous terrain everywhere.

sentences.zh: 教匪竄匿其間，劫掠而食，不煩裹糧；

translations.literal: The sect rebels hide among them, living by plunder without needing to carry provisions;
translations.idiomatic: The sect rebels hide among them, living by plunder without needing to carry provisions;

sentences.zh: 迫民前驅，不煩招集。

translations.literal: They force civilians ahead as vanguard without needing to recruit.
translations.idiomatic: They force civilians ahead as vanguard without needing to recruit.

sentences.zh: 官兵至，輒翻山越澗而逃。

translations.literal: When government troops arrive, the rebels flee over mountains and across streams.
translations.idiomatic: When government troops arrive, the rebels flee over mountains and across streams.

sentences.zh: 官兵必先運糧，又須探路，諸費周章。

translations.literal: Government troops must first transport grain and also scout the route—all expenses multiply in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops must first transport grain and also scout the route, and every expense becomes a burden.

sentences.zh: 即道路可通，餱糧可繼，而日夜追躡奔走，其勢必疲。

translations.literal: Even if the road can be opened and rations sustained, day-and-night pursuit leaves the troops exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the roads can be opened and rations sustained, day-and-night pursuit inevitably exhausts the troops.

sentences.zh: 是教匪逸而兵勞也。

translations.literal: Thus the sect rebels escape while the soldiers grow weary.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the sect rebels escape while the soldiers grow weary.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為當先嚴守要隘，俾教匪無路可奔；

translations.literal: Your servant humbly believes we should first strictly guard key passes so the sect rebels have nowhere to flee;
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe we should first strictly guard key passes so the sect rebels have nowhere to flee;

sentences.zh: 乃宣上德意，散其脅從，然後臨之以兵，分道進剿。

translations.literal: Then proclaim the emperor's benevolent intent, disperse their coerced followers, and only then confront them with troops in divided columns for suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Then proclaim the emperor's benevolent intent, disperse their coerced followers, and only then confront them with troops in divided columns for suppression.

sentences.zh: 教匪途窮食盡，計日可平。

translations.literal: When the sect rebels run out of roads and food, pacification may be counted in days.
translations.idiomatic: When the sect rebels run out of roads and food, pacification may be counted in days.

sentences.zh: 聞陝省有團練鄉勇，或一二村，或數村，聯合築堡為聲援。

translations.literal: I have heard that Shaanxi has militia and local braves—one or two villages, or several villages—uniting to build forts as mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in Shaanxi militia and local braves—one or two villages, or several villages—unite to build forts as mutual support.

sentences.zh: 川、楚可推而行之，令各守本境，俾自護其田廬婦子。

translations.literal: Sichuan and Hubei could adopt this: let each area defend its own territory so the people may protect their fields, homes, wives, and children.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan and Hubei could adopt the same practice: let each area defend its own territory so the people may protect their fields, homes, wives, and children.

sentences.zh: 則教匪雖多，驟難肆擾。

translations.literal: Then however many sect rebels there are, they cannot quickly rampage.
translations.idiomatic: Then however many sect rebels there are, they cannot quickly rampage.

sentences.zh: 官兵剿撫兼施，無顧此失彼之慮。」

translations.literal: Government troops can combine suppression and pacification without fear of attending to one front and losing another."
translations.idiomatic: Government troops can combine suppression and pacification without fear of attending to one front and losing another.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「所論極是。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "What you say is entirely correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "What you say is entirely correct.

sentences.zh: 總之能堵方能剿，能剿方能撫，大端不外乎此。」

translations.literal: In general, one must block before one can suppress, suppress before one can pacify—the main points are no more than this."
translations.idiomatic: In general, one must block before one can suppress, and suppress before one can pacify—the main points are no more than this."

sentences.zh: 尋以病乞解任，還太子太保。

translations.literal: Soon, citing illness, he requested release from office and was restored to Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, citing illness, he asked to be relieved of office and was restored to Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太傅，遣御前侍衛豐伸濟倫奠醊，諡莊敏。

translations.literal: He died; was posthumously given Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Imperial Bodyguard Feng Shenjilun was dispatched to offer libations; posthumous name Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously given Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Imperial Bodyguard Feng Shenjilun was dispatched to offer libations, and he received the posthumous name Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: 子鈺，進士，直隸清河道；

translations.literal: His son Yu passed the jinshi and served as Qinghe Circuit intendant in Zhili;
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu, a jinshi, served as Qinghe Circuit intendant in Zhili;

sentences.zh: 鏻，湖南鹽法道。

translations.literal: Lin served as Hunan salt intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Lin served as Hunan salt intendant.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：牧民於平世，自庶而求富，修水利，飭農功，其先務也。

translations.literal: =Commentary= The commentary says: To govern the people in peaceful times, moving from modest order toward prosperity, repairing waterworks and supervising agricultural labor—these are the first priorities.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: To govern the people in peaceful times, moving from modest order toward prosperity, repairing waterworks and supervising agricultural labor—these are the first priorities.

sentences.zh: 觀承殫心力於是，政行畿甸。

translations.literal: Guancheng devoted his full energy to this, and his policies took hold across the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Guancheng poured his full energy into this, and his policies took hold across the capital region.

sentences.zh: 富明安、元理、瀚皆以此為急，各著績效。

translations.literal: Fu Ming'an, Yuanli, and Han all made this urgent and each achieved notable results.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ming'an, Yuanli, and Han all made this their urgent priority and each achieved notable results.

sentences.zh: 幹貞籌運道，尤重行水。

translations.literal: Ganzhen planned the transport route and especially emphasized keeping the waterways open.
translations.idiomatic: Ganzhen planned the transport route and especially valued keeping the waterways open.

sentences.zh: 世傑起下僚，介而能恕。

translations.literal: Shijie rose from low office, upright yet able to forgive.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie rose from low office, upright yet able to forgive.

sentences.zh: 燿以學為政，所施未盡其蘊。

translations.literal: Yao took learning as his standard in governing, yet could not fully bring out all he had mastered.
translations.idiomatic: Yao took learning as his standard in governing, yet could not fully bring out all he had mastered.

sentences.zh: 季堂論治教匪，後來堅壁清野之議，已發其端。

translations.literal: Jitang's discussion of suppressing the sect rebels already opened the way for the later policy of fortifying walls and clearing the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Jitang's discussion of suppressing the sect rebels already opened the way for the later policy of fortifying walls and clearing the countryside.

sentences.zh: 我有先正，言明且清，諸臣所論列，足當之矣。

translations.literal: We have worthy forebears whose words were clear and bright; what these ministers set forth is enough to measure up to them.
translations.idiomatic: We have worthy forebears whose words were clear and bright; what these ministers set forth is enough to measure up to them.
